segments.zh: 我去了英国，在瑞士度过了一周，最后一周半，我和母亲住在一起。所以我对英国时间非常熟悉。

segments.ko: Okay. How do you deal with jet-lag?  Because you are someone who kind of travels quite a lot, and living in  Japan, living in Malaysia these days,
segments.zh: 好的。你如何应对时差反应？  因为你是一个经常旅行的人，最近住在日本、马来西亚，

segments.ko: that does involve travelling  quite long distances sometimes.
segments.zh: 有时确实需要长途旅行。

segments.ko: How do you deal with jet-lag, and do you have any kind of tips for recovering  from jet-lag or dealing with it?
segments.zh: 您如何应对时差反应？对于从时差反应中恢复或应对时差反应，您有什么建议吗？

segments.ko: I've been finding it's getting more difficult  as I get older, as we all are. So, especially
segments.zh: 我发现随着年龄的增长，事情变得越来越困难，就像我们所有人一样。所以，特别是

segments.ko: like travelling east to west, so from Asia to  Europe, time was I'd be able to just stay up
segments.zh: 就像从东到西旅行一样，从亚洲到欧洲，我可以熬夜

segments.ko: extra late for one night, and I was in European  time straight away. It takes longer these days.
segments.zh: 加晚了一晚，我马上就到了欧洲时间。这些天需要更长的时间。

segments.ko: I still think not sleeping is the key. Just  when you arrive, tell yourself it is this time,
segments.zh: 我仍然认为不睡觉是关键。当你到达时，告诉自己就是这个时候，

segments.ko: it is local time. Then try to stay in that time  as much as is possible as soon as you arrive.
segments.zh: 现在是当地时间。然后在您到达后尽可能多地停留在那个时间。

segments.ko: So this time, yeah, I flew from Kuala Lumpur  in Malaysia to Madrid, and landed about 8 p.m.,
segments.zh: 所以这一次，是的，我从马来西亚的吉隆坡飞往马德里，并于晚上 8 点左右降落，

segments.ko: which would have been very late for me, and  then stayed up as late as I could each night.
segments.zh: 这对我来说已经很晚了，然后我每晚都尽可能地熬夜。

segments.ko: But it took me maybe four or five days to  completely acclimatise to Spanish time.
segments.zh: 但我大概花了四五天的时间才完全适应西班牙时间。

segments.ko: I did find myself waking up early and  flagging in mid-evening for a few days.
segments.zh: 我确实发现自己早起，并连续几天在半夜精神萎靡。

segments.ko: Going the other way, I would say the same.  As soon as possible, tell yourself it's local
segments.zh: 换个角度看，我也会这么说。  尽快告诉自己这是本地的

segments.ko: time. So in the middle of September, I'm going  to be flying from Lisbon to Tokyo via Abu Dhabi.
segments.zh: 时间。因此，九月中旬，我将从里斯本飞往东京，经阿布扎比。

segments.ko: So as soon as I get on the plane in Abu Dhabi, I'm changing my phone to Tokyo time.  So then my head will be thinking, ah,
segments.zh: 因此，当我在阿布扎比登机时，我就把手机改成东京时间。  那么我的脑子就会想，啊，

segments.ko: it is this time. And when I arrive in Tokyo,  with luck and justice, I will be used to it.
segments.zh: 就是这一次。当我到达东京时，如果运气好、正义的话，我会习惯的。

segments.ko: Yeah. But it's extra hard going that direction, isn't it? Going from west to east  for some reason is extra punishing.
segments.zh: 是的。但朝这个方向走是非常困难的，不是吗？由于某种原因从西向东行驶是额外的惩罚。

segments.ko: I remember going from England to  Japan the second time and trying to kind of function normally straight  away. I remember taking my bike,
segments.zh: 我记得第二次从英国去日本，并试图立即恢复正常。我记得我骑着自行车，

segments.ko: my mamachari that I used to have, this big sort  of housewives bicycle that I used to ride around,
segments.zh: 我曾经拥有的我的mamachari，我曾经骑过的这种大型家庭主妇自行车，

segments.ko: taking that down to the local supermarket,  filling up the baskets of my bike with stuff and
segments.zh: 把它带到当地的超市，在我的自行车篮子里装满东西

segments.ko: then riding back. And I got so suddenly so drowsy  and so lightheaded that I couldn't ride the bike.
segments.zh: 然后骑马回去。我突然变得昏昏欲睡、头晕目眩，无法骑自行车。

segments.ko: I got all dizzy on the bike. I remember pushing this bike back to my apartment.  It was suddenly such a struggle.
segments.zh: 我骑着自行车就头晕了。我记得把这辆自行车推回我的公寓。  突然之间就变得如此挣扎。

segments.ko: I was hit by this wall of jet lag. But  going the other direction is not so bad for some reason. I guess you're going against the  rotation of the earth or something like that?
segments.zh: 我被这堵时差墙击中了。但出于某种原因，走向另一个方向并不是那么糟糕。我猜你是在反对地球自转或类似的东西？

segments.ko: Is that what it is?
segments.zh: 是这样吗？

segments.ko: I think it's just more disorienting going  from west to east because you sleep and
segments.zh: 我认为从西向东更容易迷失方向，因为你睡觉并且

segments.ko: you wake up and suddenly it's evening. So  it's like 8 p.m. and you're awake. When I
segments.zh: 你醒来，突然就到了晚上。现在大约是晚上 8 点。你醒了。当我

segments.ko: arrived first in Japan and we were sharing that  apartment, I had never been to Asia before.
segments.zh: 首先到达日本，我们共用那间公寓，我以前从未去过亚洲。

segments.ko: I had no clue how to deal with it. So I  just arrived in Japan. Hey, look at this.
segments.zh: 我不知道如何处理它。所以我刚到日本。嘿，看看这个。

segments.ko: And I remember one time you saw me just  curled up on my foot in the middle of the afternoon because I had just been knocked  over by the same thing, by that wall of
segments.zh: 我记得有一次你在下午看到我蜷缩在脚上，因为我刚刚被同样的东西撞倒了，被那堵墙撞倒了。

segments.ko: jet lag. Suddenly it just became impossible  to stay awake. My body said, no, sleep time.
segments.zh: 时差反应。突然之间，我变得无法保持清醒。我的身体说，不，是睡觉时间。

segments.ko: Yeah, exactly. You just shut down.
segments.zh: 是的，完全正确。你刚刚关闭。

segments.ko: But you're right. The best way is just  to, as soon as possible, start operating on local time. Make your mind think that it is  local time and just adapt as much as you can.
segments.zh: 但你是对的。最好的方法就是尽快开始按当地时间运营。让您的大脑认为现在是当地时间，并尽可能适应。

segments.ko: I've heard that there are things you can take.  I can't remember what it is now, but apparently
segments.zh: 我听说有些东西是可以拿走的。  我不记得现在是什么了，但显然

segments.ko: you can sort of take drops or pills even that kind  of help you adapt. Something to do with sunlight.
segments.zh: 您可以服用滴剂或药片来帮助您适应。跟阳光有关系。

segments.ko: What's the word? There's a chemical.
segments.zh: 词是什么？有一种化学物质。

segments.ko: Is that melatonin?
segments.zh: 那是褪黑激素吗？

segments.ko: Melatonin, right. I've heard that you can take  melatonin that helps. Not sure if it's true.
segments.zh: 褪黑激素，对吧。我听说您可以服用褪黑激素，这会有所帮助。不确定这是否属实。

segments.ko: Yeah, I would be wary of doing that.  I just trust my body to know what it's doing. As much as possible, I try  not to medicalise things and not
segments.zh: 是的，我会对此保持警惕。  我只是相信我的身体知道它在做什么。我尽可能不将事情医疗化，也不

segments.ko: to take medicine when my body's  able to deal with it by itself.
segments.zh: 当我的身体能够自行处理时才吃药。

segments.ko: I just power through the jet  lag until I'm in the right time.
segments.zh: 我只是克服时差，直到到达正确的时间。

segments.ko: Yeah, that's the thing. That's the key. So  you're back in the UK then after, I mean, you do visit occasionally, but most of  your time is spent these days in Malaysia,
segments.zh: 是的，就是这样。这就是关键。所以你回到英国之后，我的意思是，你偶尔会去英国，但这些天你大部分时间都花在马来西亚，

segments.ko: but yes, long time in Japan as well.
segments.zh: 但是，是的，在日本也呆了很长时间。

segments.ko: But being back in the UK now, what strikes you as being different? Do you  ever get that feeling of reverse culture shock?
segments.zh: 但现在回到英国，您觉得有何不同？您是否有过逆向文化冲击的感觉？

segments.ko: It's a weird one, isn't it? Because  first Japan and now Malaysia, they became my points of reference. So when I  go anywhere, I'm comparing it with Malaysia now.
segments.zh: 这很奇怪，不是吗？因为首先是日本，现在是马来西亚，它们成为了我的参考点。因此，当我去任何地方时，我都会将其与马来西亚进行比较。

segments.ko: So coming back to the UK, everything seems  strange and different and somehow familiar. So
segments.zh: 所以回到英国，一切看起来都很奇怪、不同，但又有些熟悉。所以

segments.ko: it's an odd one. Something that has jumped out  at me straight away is the advertising on TV.
segments.zh: 这很奇怪。电视上的广告立刻引起了我的注意。

segments.ko: It has become much more forthright.
segments.zh: 它变得更加直率了。

segments.ko: Yeah, really?
segments.zh: 是啊，真的吗？

segments.ko: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.ko: There's an advert on TV for an  all over deodorant body spray.
segments.zh: 电视上有一则全身除臭身体喷雾剂的广告。

segments.ko: And in big letters on the screen,  they're saying, boobs, balls, butts.
segments.zh: 屏幕上用大字写着：胸部、蛋蛋、屁股。

segments.ko: Yeah, really?
segments.zh: 是啊，真的吗？

segments.ko: Yes. And people are spraying this  spray down their pants and people are sniffing each other's butts  and crotches. And it's very weird.
segments.zh: 是的。人们把这种喷雾喷在裤子上，人们互相闻对方的屁股和胯部。这很奇怪。

segments.ko: Because you wouldn't get that in  Malaysia, something so blatantly, so outrageously kind of sexualised.
segments.zh: 因为在马来西亚你不会看到这种如此公然、如此令人愤慨的性化行为。

segments.ko: Exactly. It is a much more conservative  society. So that was a surprise for me.
segments.zh: 确切地。这是一个更加保守的社会。所以这对我来说是一个惊喜。

segments.ko: Yeah, it must be weird for some visitors going  to the UK where you do see things like that, that seems so kind of sexually  explicit or permissive. Certain
segments.zh: 是的，对于一些去英国的游客来说一定很奇怪，在那里你确实看到了这样的事情，这似乎是一种露骨或纵容的性行为。肯定

segments.ko: things about our culture must  be so kind of shocking. Yeah.
segments.zh: 我们文化中的事情一定令人震惊。是的。

segments.ko: I remember going after living in Japan, you know,  for a relatively short time really compared to how
segments.zh: 我记得在日本生活的时间相对较短，与之前相比

segments.ko: long you've been living away. And I'd been away  for maybe 18 months. And I went back in August, and I was struck by how, how green  everything is, even in London.
segments.zh: 你已经离开家很久了。我已经离开了大约 18 个月。我八月份回去了，我对一切都是如此、如此绿色感到震惊，即使在伦敦也是如此。

segments.ko: And I'd been living, you know, just outside Tokyo.  And yeah, just how kind of green everything is always strikes me. Even now, I live in  Paris, which is not really that far away.
segments.zh: 你知道，我一直住在东京郊外。  是的，一切的绿色总是让我印象深刻。即使现在，我也住在巴黎，距离并不远。

segments.ko: But yeah, going back to England, everything  seems so lush and green. And even in, in towns like Warwick, where my parents  live, or other towns in England,
segments.zh: 但是，是的，回到英格兰，一切看起来都是那么郁郁葱葱。甚至在我父母居住的沃里克这样的城镇，或者英格兰的其他城镇，

segments.ko: you get this sense that there's so much greenery  that's growing, you see kind of brick walls, and there's moss growing on the wall, or  there are, you know, there's pavements. And
segments.zh: 你会感觉到有很多绿色植物正在生长，你会看到砖墙，墙上长满了青苔，或者，你知道，有人行道。和

segments.ko: then at the edge of the pavements, there's  grass growing out from the gaps and things.
segments.zh: 然后在人行道的边缘，有草从缝隙和东西中长出来。

segments.ko: It always seems so kind of lush.  Do you get that feeling as well?
segments.zh: 它总是显得那么茂盛。  你也有这样的感觉吗？

segments.ko: I do. Absolutely. Yeah.
segments.zh: 我愿意。绝对地。是的。

segments.ko: Like we've, we've had warm, dry, sunny weather for  the last few days. But then a couple of days ago, like the rain came back. And I think  that the climate does impact that.
segments.zh: 和我们一样，过去几天天气温暖、干燥、阳光明媚。但几天前，雨又回来了。我认为气候确实会影响这一点。

segments.ko: Because I live in Hemel Hempstead, like a new town suburb of London. It is  very residential. But everywhere there's
segments.zh: 因为我住在赫默尔亨普斯特德，就像伦敦的一个新郊区。这是非常住宅化的。但到处都有

segments.ko: trees and bushes and little patches of  grass and playing fields and open spaces.
segments.zh: 树木、灌木丛、小片草地、运动场和开放空间。

segments.ko: Like five minutes walk away, I've got the  village green, where you've got people playing cricket in good weather. And that  is ringed by trees. So it is everywhere.
segments.zh: 步行大约五分钟即可抵达村庄绿地，天气好的时候人们可以在那里打板球。那是被树木包围的。所以它无处不在。

segments.ko: I think it doesn't jump out at me as much now  because Malaysia is also staggeringly green.
segments.zh: 我想现在我已经不再那么在意了，因为马来西亚的绿色环境也令人惊叹。

segments.ko: Kuala Lumpur is like a very urbanised,  but also like everywhere in KL, you've got lush greenery. There's like  a big, big park and botanical garden.
segments.zh: 吉隆坡就像一个高度城市化的城市，但也像吉隆坡的任何地方一样，都有郁郁葱葱的绿色植物。那里就像一个很大很大的公园和植物园。

segments.ko: Even the busy, busy roads have got  trees and grasses along the of them.
segments.zh: 即使是繁忙的道路，沿途也有树木和草地。

segments.ko: I remember first time I visited, I took a  picture, which I'm still entertained by.
segments.zh: 我记得第一次来的时候，我拍了一张照片，至今仍让我印象深刻。

segments.ko: So in the background, you've got like  the Petronas towers and KL tower.
segments.zh: 因此，在背景中，您可以看到双子塔和吉隆坡塔。

segments.ko: And in the foreground, you've  got a big patch of green, like grassy land with a couple  of cows grazing on it. Wow.
segments.zh: 在前景中，你有一大片绿色，就像草地上有几头牛在上面吃草。哇。

segments.ko: Isn't it true that there  is technically a rainforest within a building there? I read about it.
segments.zh: 从技术上讲，那里的建筑物内不是真的有雨林吗？我读到过。

segments.ko: Possibly. I don't know that it's within a  building, but certainly at the base of KL tower,
segments.zh: 可能吧。我不知道它是在建筑物内，但肯定是在吉隆坡塔的底部，

segments.ko: there is a small patch of rainforest, which I  have done a little walking tour of. It isn't big.
segments.zh: 有一小片雨林，我徒步游览了那里。它不大。

segments.ko: It doesn't take long to get around, but it is wild. It is lush and there  are like monkeys living in it. Right.
segments.zh: 绕圈时间并不长，但很狂野。它郁郁葱葱，里面像猴子一样生活。正确的。

segments.ko: Do you see the monkeys then sometimes?  When I went there, I did. Yeah.
segments.zh: 你有时会看到猴子吗？  当我去那里时，我做到了。是的。

segments.ko: Okay. What kind of monkeys are they? Small ones.
segments.zh: 好的。它们是什么种类的猴子？小的。

segments.ko: I don't know exactly what kind, but  yeah, they're small little things.
segments.zh: 我不知道具体是什么类型，但是，是的，它们都是小东西。

segments.ko: Not gibbons or apes or chimpanzees or  anything like that. Possibly macaques.
segments.zh: 不是长臂猿、猿、黑猩猩或类似的动物。可能是猕猴。

segments.ko: Right. Just kind of steal your  lunch kind of little ones. Yes.
segments.zh: 正确的。只是偷了你们小孩子们的午餐。是的。

segments.ko: Yeah. Okay. Going back to the UK then,  do you miss anything about the UK?
segments.zh: 是的。好的。那么回到英国，你有想念英国的什么吗？

segments.ko: I mean, you live away, you know,  long term now. So, you know, you've obviously chosen to live away from the  place, but is there anything that you miss?
segments.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，你现在长期住在外面。所以，你知道，你显然选择了远离这个地方居住，但是你有什么想念的吗？

segments.ko: A couple of things. Yeah. I mean, I like  my football and I like my music and I do miss being able to see good quality live  football and good quality live music.
segments.zh: 有几件事。是的。我的意思是，我喜欢我的足球，我喜欢我的音乐，我确实怀念能够看到高质量的现场足球比赛和高质量的现场音乐。

segments.ko: In Japan, we could go see the local team. We could  go see Shonan Belmonte and it wasn't premiership
segments.zh: 在日本，我们可以去看当地的团队。我们可以去看湘南贝尔蒙特，但那不是英超联赛

segments.ko: quality, but it was fun to be in the stadium and  be among the fans and get the atmosphere. Yeah.
segments.zh: 质量，但在体育场里和球迷在一起并感受气氛很有趣。是的。

segments.ko: I've been to one game in Malaysia. I made a  friend who actually works for the Asian Soccer Federation. And so she scored us a couple  of tickets for like the King's Cup final,
segments.zh: 我在马来西亚看过一场比赛。我结识了一位实际上为亚洲足球联合会工作的朋友。所以她给我们买了几张国王杯决赛的门票，

segments.ko: like the equivalent of the FA Cup final that  was held at the National Stadium, 70,000 people.
segments.zh: 就像在国家体育场举行的足总杯决赛一样，有 70,000 人。

segments.ko: And it was full, it was rammed. Yeah.  In England, the game is the spectacle.
segments.zh: 它已经满了，被夯实了。是的。  在英格兰，比赛就是一场奇观。

segments.ko: So we go and we watch the  game and we sing our sweary, violent songs. Yeah. Certainly this  game, it was more like entertainment.
segments.zh: 所以我们就去看比赛，唱着脏话、暴力的歌曲。是的。当然这个游戏，它更像是一种娱乐。

segments.ko: So there was a pre-game show with  singing and dancing and like even an hour and a half before the  game started, before kickoff,
segments.zh: 所以在比赛开始前一个半小时，在开球前，有一场载歌载舞的赛前表演，

segments.ko: they were just blasting this mad loud music  everywhere in the stadium. So me and my friend, we couldn't actually talk with each other  because the music was so loud. Whoa.
segments.zh: 他们只是在体育场各处播放这种疯狂而吵闹的音乐。所以我和我的朋友实际上无法互相交谈，因为音乐太大声了。哇哦。

segments.ko: Yeah. The game was marred by a  partial referee. A partial referee?
segments.zh: 是的。比赛因裁判不公正而受到损害。部分裁判？

segments.ko: Yeah.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.ko: Like the referee seemed to be  favouring the big side. Oh, so the referee was kind of  biassed to the big team? Yeah.
segments.zh: 就像裁判似乎偏向大方一样。哦，所以裁判对大球队有点偏见？是的。

segments.ko: Oh, right.
segments.zh: 哦，对了。

segments.ko: That's not good, is it? It wasn't, no.  Because you had like the main team, which were, I forgot their name, and like  another mid-table team called Telanganu.
segments.zh: 这不太好吧？不是，不。  因为你们有像主队一样的球队，我忘了他们的名字，还有另一支中游球队叫特兰加努队。

segments.ko: And this is something that jumped out  at me as because Kuala Lumpur is very
segments.zh: 这让我突然意识到，因为吉隆坡非常

segments.ko: multicultural. In Malaysia, it's something  like 70 or 80% Malay people, 20% Chinese,
segments.zh: 多元文化。在马来西亚，大约 70 或 80% 是马来人，20% 是华人，

segments.ko: 10% Indian. That's not exactly right,  but loosely, those are the proportions.
segments.zh: 10% 印度人。这并不完全正确，但粗略地说，这些就是比例。

segments.ko: The Chinese and the Indians are  concentrated in the main cities, but Telanganu is out in the countryside. It's in  the northeast of the country. It's pretty rural.
segments.zh: 中国人和印度人集中在主要城市，但特兰加努人则在乡村。它位于该国东北部。真是很乡村啊。

segments.ko: So when I was on the train going to  the stadium with the Telanganu fans, it was 100% Malay people. Yeah.  So that really jumped out at me.
segments.zh: 所以当我和 Telanganu 球迷一起坐火车去体育场时，100% 都是马来人。是的。  这真的让我大吃一惊。

segments.ko: Right. Yeah. It gave you an idea of the  kind of ethnic makeup of the country.
segments.zh: 正确的。是的。它让您了解这个国家的民族构成。

segments.ko: That's right. Yeah. Because like I've  travelled to a few places around Malaysia, but only really to the bigger and  more built up cities and towns.
segments.zh: 这是正确的。是的。因为就像我去过马来西亚周围的一些地方一样，但只去过更大、更发达的城镇。

segments.ko: So I've not been out to the real  countryside, more remote areas.
segments.zh: 所以我还没有去过真正的乡村，更偏远的地区。

segments.ko: Okay. So football and music. Do they not have  the same kind of live music scene over there?
segments.zh: 好的。所以足球和音乐。他们那里没有同样的现场音乐场景吗？

segments.ko: I'm slowly finding it. For example, in Japan,  in Tokyo, or in England, there's lots of music
segments.zh: 我正在慢慢寻找。例如，在日本、东京或英国，有很多音乐

segments.ko: happening everywhere all the time. I can  find lots of the noisy rock that I like.
segments.zh: 每时每刻都在发生。我可以找到很多我喜欢的吵闹的摇滚乐。

segments.ko: Noisy rock seems less common  in Malaysia. In Southeast Asia, generally, there's a preference for  pop music. So rock of the kind I like,
segments.zh: 喧闹的摇滚乐在马来西亚似乎不太常见。在东南亚，人们普遍偏爱流行音乐。所以我喜欢的那种摇滚，

segments.ko: the weird, noisy psychedelic stuff,  is very much a minority taste.
segments.zh: 奇怪、吵闹、迷幻的东西，在很大程度上是少数人的口味。

segments.ko: I have found a couple of bands. There  was one band I saw. It was fantastic.
segments.zh: 我找到了几个乐队。我看到了一支乐队。太棒了。

segments.ko: It was a bunch of middle-aged Indian men playing  noisy, noisy hard rock. Wow. It was fantastic.
segments.zh: 那是一群中年印度男人在演奏吵闹的硬摇滚。哇。太棒了。

segments.ko: Oh, that's great. It does exist. I'm finding a  few bands that I'd be interested to go and see.
segments.zh: 哦，那太好了。它确实存在。我正在寻找一些我有兴趣去看的乐队。

segments.ko: But yeah, the scene seems to be much  more about pop and jazz and classical, less about horrible, noisy rock.
segments.zh: 但是，是的，这个场景似乎更多地是关于流行乐、爵士乐和古典乐，而不是关于可怕、吵闹的摇滚乐。

segments.ko: I wonder why that is. Why horrible,  noisy rock is not sweeping the nation.
segments.zh: 我想知道这是为什么。为什么可怕、吵闹的摇滚乐没有席卷全国。

segments.ko: It's much easier to find in Japan. In Tokyo,  I could go on tokyogigguide.com and have no trouble finding noise or abstract or  experimental. I would happily gamble
segments.zh: 在日本更容易找到。在东京，我可以访问 tokyogigguide.com，轻松找到噪音、抽象或实验性内容。我很乐意赌博

segments.ko: two or three thousand yen on a concert  just for the sake of actually going to the show and being in the space and having  the experience of seeing the live music.
segments.zh: 一场音乐会花上两三千日元，只是为了真正去现场观看演出，身处现场，体验一下现场音乐。

segments.ko: Fairly often it would be good,  and sometimes it would not be.
segments.zh: 通常情况下这会很好，但有时则不然。

segments.ko: But it's interesting that in Japan, you do  find all this kind of alternative music. It's a really vibrant scene for all different  types of alternative music. And yet,
segments.zh: 但有趣的是，在日本，你确实可以找到所有此类另类音乐。对于所有不同类型的另类音乐来说，这都是一个充满活力的场景。然而，

segments.ko: apparently in Kuala Lumpur,  this is not so much the case.
segments.zh: 显然在吉隆坡，情况并非如此。

segments.ko: I wonder why. What could be the reason for that?
segments.zh: 我想知道为什么。原因可能是什么？

segments.ko: No idea. Just speculating off the top of  my head, it could be outside influence.
segments.zh: 不知道。只是我的猜测，这可能是外部影响。

segments.ko: Japan was not completely occupied by the  U.S., but in the post-war years, there had
segments.zh: 日本并未完全被美国占领，但在战后的岁月里，

segments.ko: been a heavy U.S. influence on Japanese social  culture just from the presence of the troops
segments.zh: 仅从军队的存在来看，美国就对日本社会文化产生了重大影响

segments.ko: bringing all their food and music and movies  and what have you. So that is one possibility.
segments.zh: 带来他们所有的食物、音乐和电影以及你拥有的一切。所以这是一种可能性。

segments.ko: Yeah, similar to the U.K. in a way. Because  post-war, the U.K. was flooded by American pop
segments.zh: 是的，在某种程度上类似于英国。因为战后，英国充斥着美国流行音乐

segments.ko: culture, and that includes a lot of our music. And  so you've got a kind of rock and roll scene which
segments.zh: 文化，其中包括我们的很多音乐。所以你就有了一种摇滚场景

segments.ko: sort of developed into its own thing with stuff  like Mersey Beat in Liverpool and other forms.
segments.zh: 像利物浦的 Mersey Beat 和其他形式一样，它已经发展成为自己的东西。

segments.ko: And in fact, what eventually happened  is that the U.K. sent American music and culture back to America and was very  successful with that. You can sort of see
segments.zh: 事实上，最终发生的事情是英国将美国音乐和文化带回了美国，并且非常成功。你可以看到

segments.ko: how Japan was influenced in a similar  way as well, and as a result kind of expanded into these different genres  of music. Yeah, I can see that.
segments.zh: 日本也受到类似的影响，并因此扩展到这些不同的音乐流派。是的，我看得出来。

segments.ko: Going back to the U.K. again one more time, are there things that you don't miss  about Britain, about life in England?
segments.zh: 再次回到英国，关于英国、关于英格兰的生活，有哪些事情是您不会怀念的吗？

segments.ko: I don't get tired of being  warm. I like that. Yeah.
segments.zh: 我不会厌倦温暖。我喜欢这样。是的。

segments.ko: Yeah, so it does rain in KL, but it's generally  a quick downpour at the end of the afternoon.
segments.zh: 是的，吉隆坡确实下雨了，但通常在下午快结束时就会下倾盆大雨。

segments.ko: Yeah, I was going to ask actually  what the kind of seasons are like.
segments.zh: 是的，我实际上想问季节是什么样的。

segments.ko: Because in England, of course, winter, cold, dark, often wet. You don't see the sun for a  good three or four months, it feels like.
segments.zh: 当然，因为在英格兰，冬天寒冷、黑暗，而且经常潮湿。感觉上你已经有三四个月看不到太阳了。

segments.ko: And then spring comes along. Spring is  wonderful. It's never really that hot, but you get showers and sunshine  and everything comes to life.
segments.zh: 然后春天来了。春天是美好的。天气从来没有那么热，但你会有阵雨和阳光，一切都会变得生机勃勃。

segments.ko: Summer is typically dry and hot, although  you do get summer rain. And then, you know, the autumn, things cool down, you can  get lovely sunshine and stuff like
segments.zh: 夏季通常干燥炎热，但也会下雨。然后，你知道，到了秋天，天气变凉了，你可以享受到可爱的阳光和诸如此类的东西

segments.ko: that. But it's generally sort of dry  in the summer and wet in the winter.
segments.zh: 那。但通常夏季干燥，冬季潮湿。

segments.ko: Japan, it's kind of the opposite. So in winter, it's often very dry. It's  cold, but it's extremely dry.
segments.zh: 日本则恰恰相反。所以在冬天，天气往往非常干燥。天气很冷，但非常干燥。

segments.ko: The sky is often beautifully blue. And then you  get in, after a lovely sunny spring, you get
segments.zh: 天空常常是美丽的蓝色。然后你进去，在一个阳光明媚的春天之后，你会得到

segments.ko: that kind of rainy season where for a month, it  rains all the time. It gets more and more humid.
segments.zh: 那种雨季，整整一个月，一直下雨。天气变得越来越潮湿。

segments.ko: And then the summer arrives and it's boiling  hot, really humid and really difficult, I found. And then big storms  happen at the end of summer.
segments.zh: 然后夏天到来了，天气非常炎热，非常潮湿，而且非常困难，我发现。然后夏末就会发生大风暴。

segments.ko: You get all these big storms and stuff and a  lot of rain and wind and electrical storms.
segments.zh: 你会遇到所有这些大风暴和东西，以及大量的雨、风和雷暴。

segments.ko: And then you kind of go back to that dry,  colder weather. What about in Malaysia then?
segments.zh: 然后你就会回到那种干燥、寒冷的天气。那么在马来西亚呢？

segments.ko: Matthew Tracey It's tropical. It's hot  and humid all the time. Mildly humid, like not anything like as humid as the  Japanese summer, because that was horrendous.
segments.zh: 马修·特雷西 这里是热带地区。一直又热又湿。温和潮湿，不像日本夏天那样潮湿，因为那太可怕了。

segments.ko: I live in Malaysia. I've been to Singapore,  Vietnam, Myanmar, Thailand, and I have never,
segments.zh: 我住在马来西亚。我去过新加坡、越南、缅甸、泰国，但从未去过，

segments.ko: ever suffered humidity as badly  as Kyoto in summer. It was rank.
segments.zh: 夏天的时候，这里的湿度和京都一样严重。这是等级。

segments.ko: I wasn't dry for a week.
segments.zh: 我一周都没干。

segments.ko: It was horrible. Neil Milliken Yeah. I remember in  Japan, people would even, you know, I heard people
segments.zh: 太可怕了。尼尔·米利肯 是的。我记得在日本，人们甚至会，你知道，我听到人们

segments.ko: talking about, I would ask my students, like, how  do you deal with this kind of hot, humid weather?
segments.zh: 说到这里，我会问我的学生，比如，你们如何应对这种炎热潮湿的天气？

segments.ko: Constantly asking the students, you know,  for their advice and their experiences.
segments.zh: 你知道，不断询问学生的建议和经验。

segments.ko: And people would talk about your  clothes, because they get damp.
segments.zh: 人们会谈论你的衣服，因为它们会湿。

segments.ko: Even the clothes in your cupboards would  get damp, and they would even get mouldy.
segments.zh: 就连柜子里的衣服也会受潮，甚至会发霉。

segments.ko: So I would hear about people having mould grow on  their clothes. And so they would buy silica gel in
segments.zh: 所以我会听说有人的衣服上长了霉菌。所以他们会购买硅胶

segments.ko: large bags and put silica gel in their cupboards  and things to absorb all of the moisture.
segments.zh: 大袋子并将硅胶放入橱柜和物品中以吸收所有水分。

segments.ko: Matthew Tracey Yeah, I can totally see  that. Because until I came back in May, I was like renting a room in  a shared apartment in Kuala
segments.zh: 马修·特雷西 是的，我完全明白这一点。因为直到五月份我回来之前，我就像在瓜拉的合租公寓里租了一个房间

segments.ko: Lumpur. And I kept a few things just  in a suitcase on top of the wardrobe.
segments.zh: 吉隆坡。我把一些东西放在衣柜顶上的手提箱里。

segments.ko: And when at the start of May, I  came to open the suitcase, yeah, there was mould growing on a couple of things.
segments.zh: 五月初，当我打开手提箱时，是的，有几件东西上长了霉菌。

segments.ko: Neil Milliken Yeah, I mean,  that's crazy for us. You know, it's just like something that never  happens. You'd never experienced that.
segments.zh: 尼尔·米利肯：是的，我的意思是，这对我们来说太疯狂了。你知道，这就像从未发生过的事情一样。你从来没有经历过。

segments.ko: But yeah, that was a weird thing.  So okay, so it's hot and humid, then all year round, you don't get like a, it's  not seasonal, you don't get colder periods and,
segments.zh: 但是，是的，那是一件奇怪的事情。  好吧，所以天气又热又湿，那么一年四季，你都不会像这样，这不是季节性的，你不会遇到寒冷的时期，而且，

segments.ko: and warmer periods, it's just more or  less kind of the same thing all the time.
segments.zh: 在温暖的时期，情况或多或少都是一样的。

segments.ko: Matthew Tracey More or less the same year round.  I haven't clocked the seasons completely yet,
segments.zh: 马修·特雷西 (Matthew Tracey) 全年大致相同。  我还没完全统计好季节

segments.ko: because I haven't lived a complete year yet  in Malaysia. There are times of year when it gets slightly hotter and slightly  more humid, and it rains a bit more.
segments.zh: 因为我在马来西亚还没有住满一年。一年中的某些时候，天气会变得稍微热一点、潮湿一点，雨也会多一些。

segments.ko: But the difference is one of degree,  not actual substance. Yeah, okay. Okay.
segments.zh: 但区别只是程度不同，而非实质内容。是啊，好吧。好的。

segments.ko: So basically, it's more or  less the same year round.
segments.zh: 所以基本上，一年四季都差不多。

segments.ko: Neil Milliken So you don't miss that feeling of  always being a bit chilly in England or being in
segments.zh: 尼尔·米利肯（Neil Milliken）所以你不会怀念在英格兰或在英国总是有点冷的感觉

segments.ko: your home and there being a draft coming from  the window. And having to like put on an extra
segments.zh: 你家有风从窗户吹进来。并且不得不喜欢额外穿上

segments.ko: layer or pair of socks to keep yourself warm.  You don't have to worry about that, do you?
segments.zh: 穿一层或一双袜子以保持温暖。  你不必担心这个，不是吗？

segments.ko: Matthew Tracey Don't miss that a bit. No. Um, like the only times I ever wear long trousers  in Malaysia is to work or to be on stage.
segments.zh: 马修·特雷西 别错过这一点。不，嗯，就像我在马来西亚唯一穿长裤的时候就是工作或上舞台。

segments.ko: That's the only times.
segments.zh: 这是仅有的几次。

segments.ko: Neil Milliken On stage. Matthew Tracey Yeah.  Neil Milliken When you're doing a stand up.
segments.zh: 尼尔·米利肯在舞台上。马修·特雷西 是的。  尼尔·米利肯 当你站起来时。

segments.ko: Matthew Tracey Yeah, no  shorts. No shorts on stage.
segments.zh: 马修·特雷西 是的，不穿短裤。舞台上不能穿短裤。

segments.ko: Is that why not? It's, it's kind of an unspoken  rule in stand up. The feeling is that if you're
segments.zh: 这是为什么不呢？这是站立中的一种不成文的规则。感觉是如果你

segments.zh: 舞台上的某些东西看起来与观众不一样，那么它就需要成为表演的一部分。

segments.ko: Neil Milliken Meaning if they can see your  knees, you need to make a joke about it. Yeah,
segments.zh: 尼尔·米利肯的意思是，如果他们能看到你的膝盖，你就需要开个玩笑。是的，

segments.ko: something like that. So if I go on stage wearing  a funny hat, then I need to talk about the hat.
segments.zh: 类似的事情。因此，如果我戴着一顶滑稽的帽子上台，那么我需要谈论帽子。

segments.ko: Otherwise, the audience is going to be thinking, why is he wearing that hat? And be  distracted from my fantastic jokes.
segments.zh: 不然观众会想，他为什么要戴那顶帽子？并分散我的精彩笑话的注意力。

segments.ko: Right. Yeah. Okay.
segments.zh: 正确的。是的。好的。

segments.ko: And similarly, if you go up there with funny  looking knees, you have to make sure that your material is funnier than the knees that  they can see. Exactly. Yeah.
segments.zh: 同样，如果你带着看起来很滑稽的膝盖去那里，你必须确保你的材料比他们看到的膝盖更有趣。确切地。是的。

segments.ko: And my knees are pretty fucking funny.  So. Really? Knobbly? Knobbly knees?
segments.zh: 我的膝盖真是太搞笑了。  所以。真的吗？肿块？膝盖肿了？

segments.ko: Yep. Um, yeah, your audience should be glad that  this is on your audio recording. Yeah, there's no camera. There's  no knee camera for this. No, no.
segments.zh: 是的。嗯，是的，您的观众应该很高兴这是您的录音。是的，没有相机。没有膝关节摄像头可以做到这一点。不，不。

segments.ko: Okay. I only ever did stand  up in shorts once. Yeah.
segments.zh: 好的。我只穿着短裤站过一次。是的。

segments.ko: And yeah, I bombed. Maybe that's it.  Maybe it's because they could see my knees and they were like, well, look,  we just can't laugh at your jokes,
segments.zh: 是的，我轰炸了。也许就是这样。  也许是因为他们可以看到我的膝盖，他们说，好吧，看，我们只是不能笑你的笑话，

segments.ko: Luke, because for some reason, if we  can see the lower half of your legs, then it doesn't matter what you're saying, no  matter how hilarious, it's just not going to work.
segments.zh: 卢克，因为出于某种原因，如果我们能看到你的下半腿，那么无论你说什么，无论多么搞笑，都是行不通的。

segments.ko: Funny that.
segments.zh: 有趣的是。

segments.ko: Neil Milliken I have done that  occasionally. So on some of the few occasions I've performed in shorts, I  have like made a joke about the legs. Yeah.
segments.zh: 尼尔·米利肯 我偶尔也会这样做。因此，在我穿着短裤表演的少数场合中，我喜欢拿腿开玩笑。是的。

segments.ko: So front row ladies, hold yourselves  back. I don't feel safe. Yeah, right.
segments.zh: 所以前排的女士们，请保持冷静。我感觉不安全。是的，对。

segments.ko: Like, I don't think that's all the  psychology. I think there may be something about, you don't look authoritative  in shorts. Matthew Tracey Yeah, it's true.
segments.zh: 就像，我不认为这就是心理学的全部。我认为可能是因为，你穿着短裤看起来不具有权威性。马修·特雷西 是的，确实如此。

segments.ko: It's true. If you go on stage in shorts, the audience is going to think, you look  stupid. Why should we listen to you?
segments.zh: 这是真的。如果你穿着短裤登上舞台，观众会认为你看起来很愚蠢。我们为什么要听你的？

segments.ko: Matthew Tracey Yeah, you haven't made an effort.
segments.zh: 马修·特雷西 是的，你还没有努力。

segments.zh: 没错，你必须努力。  这是真实的。你必须得体。

segments.ko: If you're going to go up on stage  and expect people to listen to you, you've got to make some effort. Yeah. And  at least covering your legs, at least.
segments.zh: 如果您要走上舞台并期望人们倾听您的意见，您就必须做出一些努力。是的。至少遮住你的腿。

segments.ko: Yeah, I mean, it's not in every case. There's a  comedian, an Irish guy who's based in Bangkok,
segments.zh: 是的，我的意思是，并非所有情况都是如此。有一个喜剧演员，一个住在曼谷的爱尔兰人，

segments.ko: but I saw him when he came to Malaysia, a guy  called Wes Dalton. And being like wacky and
segments.zh: 但当他来到马来西亚时我见到了他，一个叫韦斯·道尔顿的人。又像古怪的

segments.ko: very energetic and friendly and smiley and  really talking to the audience is his act.
segments.zh: 非常有活力、友好、面带微笑，真正与观众交谈是他的表演。

segments.ko: So for him, the shorts and the bright  shirt works, because it matches his onstage persona. Matthew Tracey Right.  But for most people, that wouldn't work.
segments.zh: 所以对他来说，短裤和明亮的衬衫很合适，因为它符合他在舞台上的形象。马修·特雷西 对。  但对于大多数人来说，这是行不通的。

segments.ko: Jimmy Carr in shorts wouldn't work, because he needs to be dressed in a  way that matches his high status act.
segments.zh: 吉米·卡尔穿短裤是行不通的，因为他的着装需要符合他的高地位行为。

segments.zh: 那么，您认为在马来西亚教英语与在日本教英语有什么不同吗？你的学生是什么样的？什么
